items.headline: CLAT 2023 results declared
items.text: The Consortium of National Law Universities published the results of the Common Law Admission Test 2023, held on December 18, 2022, for admission to UG and PG law programmes at participating NLUs.

items.headline: Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Bill introduced to decriminalise offences under 42 laws
items.text: The Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Bill, 2022 was introduced in the Lok Sabha to decriminalise minor offences across 42 central Acts, largely replacing imprisonment with monetary penalties, and was referred to a Joint Parliamentary Committee.
items.why: Major ease-of-doing-business decriminalisation effort.

items.headline: Parliament passes Anti-Maritime Piracy Bill
items.text: Parliament passed the Anti-Maritime Piracy Bill, creating a domestic legal framework to prosecute piracy on the high seas, including in India's Exclusive Economic Zone, and prescribing stringent punishment for acts of piracy.
items.why: India's first dedicated anti-piracy statute.

items.headline: Parliament passes Bill renaming NDIAC as India International Arbitration Centre
items.text: Parliament passed the New Delhi International Arbitration Centre (Amendment) Bill, 2022, renaming the institution the India International Arbitration Centre. The government said the old name made the centre appear city-centric and the change reflects the aim of making India a hub of institutional arbitration.

items.headline: Supreme Court dismisses Bilkis Bano's review of ruling letting Gujarat decide convicts' remission
items.text: The Supreme Court dismissed in chambers Bilkis Bano's petition seeking review of its May 2022 judgment that held the Gujarat government competent to decide the remission pleas of the 11 men convicted for the 2002 gang rape and murders, whose premature release in August 2022 had drawn wide criticism.
items.why: Her separate writ petition challenging the remission remained pending.

items.headline: Justice Dipankar Datta sworn in as Supreme Court judge
items.text: Former Bombay High Court Chief Justice Dipankar Datta took oath as a judge of the Supreme Court, administered by CJI D.Y. Chandrachud, after the Centre notified his appointment on the Collegium's September 2022 recommendation.

items.headline: BCI schedules AIBE-XVII for February 5, 2023
items.text: The Bar Council of India announced that the All India Bar Examination XVII would be held on February 5, 2023, with online registration from December 13, 2022 to January 16, 2023. The announcement came after the Delhi High Court asked the BCI to disclose the next exam date; the previous AIBE was held in October 2021.

items.headline: Collegium deliberations cannot be disclosed under RTI: Supreme Court (Anjali Bhardwaj v. CPIO, SC)
items.text: The Supreme Court dismissed an appeal seeking disclosure under the RTI Act of the agenda and outcome of a December 12, 2018 Collegium meeting, holding that only the final resolution of the Collegium, and not tentative decisions or discussions among its members, needs to be put in the public domain.
items.why: Limits transparency claims over the Collegium's internal process.

items.headline: Parliament clears Wild Life (Protection) Amendment Bill as Rajya Sabha passes it by voice vote
items.text: The Rajya Sabha passed the Wild Life (Protection) Amendment Bill by voice vote, completing parliamentary approval after Lok Sabha passage earlier in 2022. The Bill implements India's obligations under CITES, rationalises the schedules of protected species and raises penalties.

items.headline: SC voices dismay at Law Minister's Collegium remarks and delay in clearing recommendations
items.text: Hearing a contempt plea over delays in judicial appointments, a bench of Justices S.K. Kaul and A.S. Oka told the Attorney General that the Law Minister's remarks on the Collegium 'should not have happened' and criticised the Centre for sitting on reiterated names and splitting Collegium resolutions, disturbing seniority.

items.headline: Draft Digital Personal Data Protection Bill, 2022 released for consultation
items.text: MeitY released the draft Digital Personal Data Protection Bill, 2022 for public comments, proposing obligations for data fiduciaries, rights for data principals and a Data Protection Board of India, after the earlier Personal Data Protection Bill was withdrawn in August 2022.
items.why: Precursor to the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023.

items.headline: Gujarat HC Bar abstains from work indefinitely over proposed transfer of Justice Nikhil Kariel
items.text: The Gujarat High Court Advocates Association resolved to abstain from work indefinitely to protest the Supreme Court Collegium's proposal to transfer Justice Nikhil S. Kariel to the Patna High Court, and to make representations to Supreme Court judges from Gujarat.
items.why: Part of a wave of Bar protests against judge transfers in late 2022.

items.headline: CLAT 2023 application deadline extended to November 18
items.text: The Consortium of National Law Universities extended the last date for online applications for the Common Law Admission Test 2023 to November 18, 2022, ahead of the December 18 exam.

items.headline: SC orders release of Nalini Sriharan and five other Rajiv Gandhi assassination convicts
items.text: Extending the reasoning of its May 2022 A.G. Perarivalan ruling, the Supreme Court ordered the premature release of Nalini Sriharan, R.P. Ravichandran and four other life convicts in the Rajiv Gandhi assassination case, noting the Tamil Nadu Cabinet's remission recommendation and their long incarceration.

items.headline: Justice D.Y. Chandrachud sworn in as 50th Chief Justice of India
items.text: President Droupadi Murmu administered the oath of office to Justice D.Y. Chandrachud as the 50th Chief Justice of India at Rashtrapati Bhavan, succeeding CJI U.U. Lalit.

items.headline: Supreme Court upholds 10% EWS quota by 3:2 (Janhit Abhiyan v. Union of India)
items.text: A five-judge Constitution Bench upheld the 103rd Constitutional Amendment providing up to 10% reservation for economically weaker sections in education and public employment. Justices Maheshwari, Trivedi and Pardiwala formed the majority; CJI U.U. Lalit and Justice S. Ravindra Bhat dissented on the exclusion of SC/ST/OBC poor from the quota.
items.why: Accepts economic criteria as a valid basis for reservation.

items.headline: Centre constitutes 22nd Law Commission after four years; Justice Ritu Raj Awasthi named Chairperson
items.text: The Union Government appointed former Karnataka High Court Chief Justice Ritu Raj Awasthi as Chairperson of the 22nd Law Commission of India, along with members, ending a vacancy of over four years since the 21st Commission's term ended in 2018.
items.why: Revives the key law-reform advisory body.

items.headline: Law Minister Kiren Rijiju calls Collegium system 'opaque and unaccountable'
items.text: Union Law Minister Kiren Rijiju, speaking at a media conclave, said the Collegium system of appointing judges was opaque and not accountable, and that many judges and lawyers shared this view. The remarks intensified the executive-judiciary standoff over judicial appointments.
items.why: Marked an escalation in the public dispute over the Collegium.

items.headline: IT Rules amended to create Grievance Appellate Committees for social media users
items.text: MeitY notified the IT (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Amendment Rules, 2022, providing for government-constituted Grievance Appellate Committees to hear appeals against decisions of intermediaries' grievance officers, and requiring platforms to make reasonable efforts to prevent users from posting prohibited content.
items.why: Creates a government appellate layer over platform content moderation.

items.headline: SC directs police to act suo motu against hate speech (Shaheen Abdulla v. Union of India)
items.text: The Supreme Court directed the Delhi, Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand police to register cases suo motu against hate speech without waiting for complaints, irrespective of the religion of the speaker, warning that failure would be treated as contempt of court.
items.why: Shifts responsibility onto police to proactively act against hate speech.

items.headline: President appoints Justice D.Y. Chandrachud as the 50th Chief Justice of India
items.text: The President of India appointed Justice Dhananjaya Y. Chandrachud as the next Chief Justice of India with effect from November 9, 2022, on the recommendation of outgoing CJI U.U. Lalit. His tenure runs until November 2024.
items.why: Begins one of the longer CJI tenures in recent years.

items.headline: Supreme Court suspends Bombay HC order acquitting Prof. G.N. Saibaba in UAPA case
items.text: In a special Saturday sitting, a Supreme Court bench suspended the Bombay High Court judgment of October 14, 2022 that had discharged former Delhi University professor G.N. Saibaba and others in a Maoist-links UAPA case for want of valid sanction. The accused were ordered to remain in custody pending the State's appeal.
items.why: Raised debate on the effect of invalid sanction under UAPA and on extraordinary weekend hearings.

items.headline: Split verdict in Karnataka hijab ban case (Aishat Shifa v. State of Karnataka)
items.text: A two-judge bench delivered a split verdict on the Karnataka government order enabling a ban on hijab in pre-university colleges. Justice Hemant Gupta upheld the Karnataka High Court judgment and the ban, while Justice Sudhanshu Dhulia set it aside, emphasising girls' right to education and choice. The matter was referred to the CJI for a larger bench.
items.why: Leaves the question of religious dress in educational institutions to a larger bench.

items.headline: SC Collegium discloses objections of Justices Chandrachud and Nazeer to 'circulation' method
items.text: In an unusual public statement, the Supreme Court Collegium under CJI U.U. Lalit disclosed that Justices D.Y. Chandrachud and S. Abdul Nazeer had objected to selecting Supreme Court judges by written circulation instead of a physical meeting. The process was closed without recommendations as the CJI's tenure was ending.
items.why: Rare public glimpse into internal disagreement within the Collegium.

items.headline: Centre sets up Justice K.G. Balakrishnan commission on SC status for converts
items.text: The Union Government constituted a commission headed by former Chief Justice of India K.G. Balakrishnan to examine whether Scheduled Caste status can be accorded to persons who claim historical SC lineage but have converted to religions other than Hinduism, Sikhism and Buddhism. It was given two years to report.
items.why: Bears directly on pending Supreme Court litigation on reservation benefits for Dalit Christians and Muslims.

items.headline: All women entitled to safe and legal abortion up to 24 weeks: SC in X v. Principal Secretary, Health & FW Dept.
items.text: A bench of Justices D.Y. Chandrachud, A.S. Bopanna and J.B. Pardiwala (C.A. 5802/2022) held that excluding unmarried women from abortion between 20 and 24 weeks under the MTP Rules is unconstitutional, and that 'rape' for MTP purposes includes marital rape, so married women pregnant from forced sex may also seek termination.
items.why: Expands reproductive autonomy regardless of marital status.

items.headline: Centre appoints Senior Advocate R. Venkataramani as Attorney General for India
items.text: The Centre notified the appointment of Senior Advocate R. Venkataramani as Attorney General for India for three years, succeeding K.K. Venugopal whose tenure ended on September 30, 2022. Senior Advocate Mukul Rohatgi had earlier declined the offer.

items.headline: Supreme Court begins live-streaming Constitution Bench hearings
items.text: Following a full court decision, the Supreme Court began live-streaming Constitution Bench hearings from September 27, initially via YouTube. CJI U.U. Lalit said the Court would develop its own streaming platform.
items.why: Opens the country's top constitutional hearings to the public.

items.headline: Constitution Bench begins hearing challenge to All India Bar Examination
items.text: A five-judge Constitution Bench led by Justice S.K. Kaul began hearing whether the Bar Council of India can prescribe the AIBE. Attorney General K.K. Venugopal and amicus K.V. Viswanathan argued that a pre-enrolment examination was the most appropriate model, a view the BCI supported.
items.why: Could reshape the path to enrolment for all new lawyers.

items.headline: Constitution Bench reserves judgment on EWS quota; fourth Constitution Bench set up
items.text: A five-judge Constitution Bench headed by CJI U.U. Lalit reserved its verdict on petitions challenging the 103rd Constitutional Amendment providing 10% reservation for Economically Weaker Sections, and the Court constituted a fourth Constitution Bench to hear the challenge to the 2016 demonetisation.

items.headline: DoT releases draft Indian Telecommunication Bill, 2022 to replace colonial-era telegraph laws
items.text: The Department of Telecommunications released the draft Indian Telecommunication Bill, 2022 for consultation. It seeks to replace the Indian Telegraph Act, 1885, the Indian Wireless Telegraphy Act, 1933 and the Telegraph Wires (Unlawful Possession) Act, 1950, covering licensing, spectrum assignment and national security powers.

items.headline: MHA notifies Criminal Procedure (Identification) Rules, 2022
items.text: The Ministry of Home Affairs notified rules under the Criminal Procedure (Identification) Act, 2022, specifying how police and prison officers may take measurements of convicts and arrested persons, storage of the records by the National Crime Records Bureau, and procedures for destroying records.
items.why: Brings the 2022 biometrics law into operation.

items.headline: BCI Chairman writes to CJI Lalit on non-representation of large States in Supreme Court
items.text: BCI Chairman Manan Kumar Mishra wrote to CJI U.U. Lalit that some bigger, populous States had been unrepresented in the Supreme Court for several months and urged the Collegium to prioritise elevating judges from those High Courts.

items.headline: SC grants bail to journalist Siddique Kappan in UAPA case over Hathras visit
items.text: A bench of CJI U.U. Lalit and Justice S. Ravindra Bhat granted bail to Kerala journalist Siddique Kappan, in custody since October 2020, observing that every person has the right to free expression and questioning how seeking 'justice for the Hathras girl' could be a crime.

items.headline: Supreme Court notifies new listing system for fresh cases under CJI Lalit
items.text: The Supreme Court issued a circular under which fresh matters verified between Saturday and Tuesday are listed on the next week's Monday, and those verified between Wednesday and Friday on the next week's Friday, with cause lists to be published in advance.
items.why: Aimed at predictable, time-bound listing of new cases.

items.headline: Justice U.U. Lalit sworn in as 49th Chief Justice of India
items.text: President Droupadi Murmu administered the oath of office to Justice Uday Umesh Lalit as the 49th Chief Justice of India, succeeding Justice N.V. Ramana. Justice Lalit, directly elevated from the Bar in 2014, had announced reforms in listing, mentioning and constitution bench hearings.

items.headline: Supreme Court live-streams proceedings for the first time on CJI Ramana's last working day
items.text: The Supreme Court for the first time live-streamed its proceedings, broadcasting the ceremonial bench of CJI N.V. Ramana on his last working day. The Court had accepted live-streaming in principle in 2018 in Swapnil Tripathi v. Supreme Court of India.

items.headline: Pegasus: SC-appointed committee finds malware in 5 of 29 phones, not conclusively Pegasus; says Centre did not cooperate
items.text: Reading out the findings of the technical committee overseen by Justice R.V. Raveendran, CJI N.V. Ramana said malware was found on 5 of the 29 devices examined but it could not be concluded that it was Pegasus, and that the Union Government had not cooperated with the probe.

items.headline: SC issues notice on plea challenging remission to 11 life convicts in Bilkis Bano case
items.text: The Supreme Court issued notice to the Gujarat government on petitions challenging the remission granted to 11 men serving life sentences for the gang-rape of Bilkis Bano and murder of her family members during the 2002 riots, who were released on August 15, 2022.

items.headline: SC holds 2016 Benami Act amendments cannot apply retrospectively (Union of India v. Ganpati Dealcom)
items.text: A bench headed by CJI N.V. Ramana held that the Benami Transactions (Prohibition) Amendment Act, 2016 is prospective, struck down Section 3(2) of the unamended 1988 Act as unconstitutional, and held that criminal prosecution or confiscation cannot be initiated for transactions entered into before the 2016 amendment.
items.why: Ends retrospective benami prosecutions and confiscations for pre-2016 deals.

items.headline: SC refers Shiv Sena (Uddhav v. Shinde) dispute to Constitution Bench
items.text: A bench headed by CJI N.V. Ramana referred petitions arising from the split in the Shiv Sena and the change of government in Maharashtra to a five-judge Constitution Bench, flagging issues including the correctness of the Nabam Rebia ruling on Speakers facing removal notices deciding disqualification petitions.

items.headline: Standing Committee recommends uniform law on adoption and guardianship
items.text: The Parliamentary Standing Committee on Personnel, Public Grievances, Law and Justice tabled its report on 'Review of Guardianship and Adoption Laws', recommending a single, uniform adoption law applicable to all citizens and a single guardianship law that also covers senior citizens.

items.headline: Lok Sabha passes New Delhi International Arbitration Centre (Amendment) Bill, 2022
items.text: The Lok Sabha introduced and passed the New Delhi International Arbitration Centre (Amendment) Bill, 2022, which renames the institution as the India International Arbitration Centre.

items.headline: Parliament passes Family Courts (Amendment) Bill, 2022
items.text: The Rajya Sabha passed the Family Courts (Amendment) Bill, 2022, already passed by the Lok Sabha on July 26. It extends the Family Courts Act, 1984 to Himachal Pradesh (from February 15, 2019) and Nagaland (from September 12, 2008) and retrospectively validates the establishment of family courts and all actions taken by them in those States.

items.headline: CJI N.V. Ramana recommends Justice U.U. Lalit as next Chief Justice of India
items.text: Following a letter from the Law Ministry, CJI N.V. Ramana formally recommended Justice Uday Umesh Lalit, the senior-most judge of the Supreme Court, as his successor. Justice Lalit was set for a tenure of about 74 days.

items.headline: BCI resolves to allow law graduates in other jobs to enrol provisionally, subject to resigning after AIBE
items.text: The Bar Council of India told the Supreme Court it had resolved to allow law graduates employed elsewhere to enrol provisionally and take the AIBE, on an undertaking to resign within six months of passing. Separate registers will be kept, seniority will count from the date employment ends, and those out of practice for over five years must retake the AIBE.

items.headline: Parliament passes Weapons of Mass Destruction (Amendment) Bill, 2022
items.text: The Rajya Sabha passed the Weapons of Mass Destruction and their Delivery Systems (Prohibition of Unlawful Activities) Amendment Bill, 2022, which the Lok Sabha had passed in April. The Bill bars persons from financing any prohibited activity relating to weapons of mass destruction and their delivery systems.

items.headline: SC upholds ED's powers under PMLA in Vijay Madanlal Choudhary v. Union of India
items.text: A bench of Justices A.M. Khanwilkar, Dinesh Maheshwari and C.T. Ravikumar upheld the Enforcement Directorate's powers of arrest, attachment, search and seizure under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act and the 'twin conditions' for bail, and held that supplying the ECIR to the accused is not mandatory.
items.why: Shapes money-laundering prosecutions nationwide; review later sought.

items.headline: SC grants Mohammed Zubair interim bail in all UP FIRs, transfers cases to Delhi Police
items.text: A bench of Justices D.Y. Chandrachud, Surya Kant and A.S. Bopanna ordered the immediate release of Alt News co-founder Mohammed Zubair on interim bail in all FIRs registered by Uttar Pradesh Police over his tweets, transferred them to the Delhi Police and disbanded the UP SIT, observing that the power of arrest must be used sparingly.

items.headline: 'Process is the punishment': CJI Ramana flags hasty arrests and difficulty in getting bail
items.text: Speaking at the All India Legal Services Authorities' Meet in Jaipur, CJI N.V. Ramana said that in India's criminal justice system 'the process is the punishment', pointing to hasty arrests and difficulty in obtaining bail, and noting that about 80% of the 6.1 lakh prisoners in the country are undertrials.

items.headline: Standing Committee report on Mediation Bill, 2021 recommends optional pre-litigation mediation
items.text: The Parliamentary Standing Committee on Personnel, Public Grievances, Law and Justice submitted its report on the Mediation Bill, 2021. It recommended making pre-litigation mediation optional rather than mandatory, reducing the time limit for mediation from 180 to 90 days, and adding provisions for breach of confidentiality.

items.headline: SC issues bail guidelines, urges a special Bail Act (Satender Kumar Antil v. CBI)
items.text: A bench of Justices S.K. Kaul and M.M. Sundresh held that an accused is entitled to bail where arrest was made in breach of Sections 41 and 41A CrPC, issued detailed directions on bail and arrest, and urged the Centre to consider enacting a separate law to streamline the grant of bail.
items.why: A leading precedent against unnecessary arrests and undertrial detention.

items.headline: CCPA issues guidelines barring hotels and restaurants from levying service charge by default
items.text: The Central Consumer Protection Authority issued guidelines prohibiting hotels and restaurants from automatically adding service charge to food bills. On July 20, the Delhi High Court stayed the guidelines on petitions by restaurant associations.

items.headline: SC dismisses Zakia Jafri's plea against SIT clean chit in 2002 Gujarat riots 'larger conspiracy' case
items.text: A bench of Justices A.M. Khanwilkar, Dinesh Maheshwari and C.T. Ravikumar in Zakia Ahsan Jafri v. State of Gujarat upheld the acceptance of the Special Investigation Team's closure report, which had given a clean chit to then Chief Minister Narendra Modi and others on allegations of a larger conspiracy behind the 2002 riots.

items.headline: Centre notifies Surrogacy (Regulation) Rules, 2022
items.text: The Health Ministry notified the Surrogacy (Regulation) Rules, 2022 under the Surrogacy (Regulation) Act, 2021, prescribing the medical indications for gestational surrogacy, limits on procedures, staffing requirements for clinics and mandatory insurance cover for the surrogate mother.
items.why: Operationalises India's altruistic-only surrogacy framework.

items.headline: Centre notifies new Chief Justices for five High Courts
items.text: The Centre notified the appointment of Justices Vipin Sanghi, A.A. Sayed, S.S. Shinde, Rashmin M. Chhaya and Ujjal Bhuyan as Chief Justices of the Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, Rajasthan, Gauhati and Telangana High Courts respectively, acting on the Collegium's May 17 recommendations.

items.headline: CLAT 2022 held on June 19 after postponement
items.text: The Common Law Admission Test 2022 for admission to National Law Universities was held on June 19 from 2 to 4 pm, after the Consortium of NLUs had postponed it from May. The paper was described as moderately easy and broadly on the lines of CLAT 2021.

items.headline: CIC directs Bar Council of India to publish law college inspection reports on its website
items.text: Information Commissioner Saroj Punhani directed the BCI to place inspection reports of law colleges in the public domain, rejecting its plea that the data was voluminous. The Commission held that disclosure would benefit students at large and reduce repetitive RTI applications.
items.why: Improves transparency on the quality of law colleges.

items.headline: MeitY releases draft amendments to IT Rules, 2021 expanding intermediary obligations
items.text: The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology released draft amendments to the Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021 for public comment until July 6, 2022. The draft expanded intermediaries' obligations to ensure compliance with the rules and to enforce prohibitions on unlawful content.

items.headline: SC mandates minimum 1-km eco-sensitive zone around protected forests (In Re: T.N. Godavarman Thirumulpad)
items.text: In In Re: T.N. Godavarman Thirumulpad v. Union of India (2022 LiveLaw (SC) 540), the Supreme Court directed that every protected forest, national park and wildlife sanctuary must have an eco-sensitive zone of at least one km from its boundary, with no permanent structures permitted and mining prohibited within national parks and sanctuaries.
items.why: Major environmental directive affecting development near protected areas; later modified in 2023.

items.headline: SC tells Bar Councils to actually decide complaints against advocates within one year
items.text: Hearing a contempt plea, a bench of Justices M.R. Shah and B.V. Nagarathna said issuing circulars was not enough and directed Bar Councils to dispose of complaints under Section 35 of the Advocates Act within a year, constitute panels of inquiry officers, and asked the BCI to devise a mechanism for 1,273 complaints transferred to it, with a compliance report by July 14.

items.headline: GST Council recommendations not binding on Parliament and States: SC in Union of India v. Mohit Minerals
items.text: In Union of India v. Mohit Minerals Pvt. Ltd. (C.A. No. 1390 of 2022), the Supreme Court held that GST Council recommendations have only persuasive value and are not binding on Parliament and State legislatures, which have simultaneous power to legislate on GST. It also struck down IGST levy on ocean freight in CIF imports.
items.why: A significant statement on fiscal federalism under the GST regime.

items.headline: Supreme Court orders release of Rajiv Gandhi assassination convict A.G. Perarivalan under Article 142
items.text: A bench of Justices L. Nageswara Rao, B.R. Gavai and A.S. Bopanna invoked Article 142 to order the release of A.G. Perarivalan, who had spent over three decades in prison, holding that the Tamil Nadu Governor was bound by the State Cabinet's advice on his remission plea and that the long unexplained delay in deciding it was amenable to judicial review.
items.why: Clarifies limits of gubernatorial discretion under Article 161.

items.headline: Collegium recommends new Chief Justices for five High Courts, transfer of Justice S.C. Sharma to Delhi
items.text: The Supreme Court Collegium recommended Justices Vipin Sanghi (Uttarakhand), A.A. Sayed (Himachal Pradesh), S.S. Shinde (Rajasthan), R.M. Chhaya (Gauhati) and Ujjal Bhuyan (Telangana) as Chief Justices, and the transfer of Justice Satish Chandra Sharma as Chief Justice of the Delhi High Court.

items.headline: CJI Ramana flags 22% vacancies in district judiciary at J&K High Court event
items.text: Laying the foundation stone of the new Jammu and Kashmir High Court complex in Srinagar, CJI N.V. Ramana said 22% of posts in the district judiciary were still vacant and called for immediate steps to fill them, alongside better judicial infrastructure and greater use of alternative dispute resolution.

items.headline: Supreme Court keeps sedition law (Section 124A IPC) in abeyance in S.G. Vombatkere v. Union of India
items.text: A bench of CJI N.V. Ramana and Justices Surya Kant and Hima Kohli, in W.P.(C) No. 682 of 2021, directed that Section 124A IPC be kept in abeyance while the Centre re-examines it. The Centre and States were expected not to register new sedition FIRs, and pending trials, appeals and proceedings under the provision were kept in abeyance.
items.why: First judicial freeze on the colonial-era sedition offence.

items.headline: Justices Sudhanshu Dhulia and J.B. Pardiwala sworn in as Supreme Court judges
items.text: CJI N.V. Ramana administered the oath of office to Justice Sudhanshu Dhulia, until then Chief Justice of the Gauhati High Court, and Justice J.B. Pardiwala of the Gujarat High Court, days after the Collegium recommended them. The appointments took the Supreme Court to its full sanctioned strength of 34.

items.headline: SCBA writes to CJI protesting restrictions on lawyers' use of Supreme Court facilities
items.text: SCBA President Vikas Singh wrote to CJI N.V. Ramana complaining that members of the Bar were being 'treated as complete strangers', citing curbs on auditorium use for a judge's farewell, access to the new campus, parking restrictions and non-allotment of chambers.

items.headline: SC refers Delhi-Centre dispute over control of services to Constitution Bench
items.text: A bench of CJI N.V. Ramana and Justices Surya Kant and Hima Kohli in Govt of NCT of Delhi v. Union of India (C.A. 2357/2017) referred limited questions on the interpretation of Article 239AA(3)(a) and the scope of legislative and executive power over services in Delhi to a Constitution Bench.
items.why: Sets up a Constitution Bench ruling on who controls the Delhi bureaucracy.

items.headline: PM inaugurates Joint Conference of Chief Ministers and Chief Justices of High Courts
items.text: Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the Joint Conference of Chief Ministers of States and Chief Justices of High Courts at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi, in the presence of CJI N.V. Ramana. The PM stressed technology in courts, use of local languages, reducing pendency and mediation; the conference resolved to set up state-level judicial infrastructure bodies involving Chief Ministers and Chief Justices.
items.why: Key executive-judiciary coordination forum on justice delivery and court infrastructure.

items.headline: CJI Ramana flags 388 High Court vacancies, urges High Courts to expedite proposals
items.text: Speaking at the Madras High Court, CJI N.V. Ramana said 388 of 1,104 sanctioned High Court judge posts were vacant and urged High Courts to speed up recommendations for the remaining 212 vacancies. He noted 180 recommendations had been made since he took office, of which 126 appointments were completed.

items.body: Supreme Court / Bar Council of India
items.headline: SC allows employed law graduates provisional enrolment to take AIBE (BCI v. Twinkle Rahul Mangonkar)
items.text: A bench of Justices S.K. Kaul and M.M. Sundresh approved a scheme under which law graduates in other employment may be provisionally enrolled in a separate register to take the All India Bar Examination, without any right to practise, and must choose between the job and practice within six months of clearing it. Seniority will run from the date employment is given up.
items.why: Reshapes enrolment rules for law graduates holding other jobs.

items.headline: Supreme Court orders status quo on demolition drive in Delhi's Jahangirpuri
items.text: A Supreme Court bench headed by CJI N.V. Ramana ordered status quo on the North Delhi Municipal Corporation's anti-encroachment demolition drive in Jahangirpuri, carried out days after communal clashes in the area. The order was mentioned urgently by petitioners and later extended by the Court.

items.headline: Supreme Court cancels Ashish Mishra's bail in Lakhimpur Kheri case (Jagjeet Singh v. Ashish Mishra)
items.text: A bench of CJI N.V. Ramana and Justices Surya Kant and Hima Kohli set aside the Allahabad High Court's bail to Ashish Mishra, accused in the October 2021 Lakhimpur Kheri violence, finding the High Court acted in 'tearing hurry' and ignored relevant factors. The Court stressed victims' right to be heard in criminal proceedings and remitted the bail plea for fresh hearing.
items.why: Affirms participatory rights of victims at every stage of a criminal case.

items.headline: Supreme Court upholds Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Act, 2020 in Noel Harper v. Union of India
items.text: A bench of Justices A.M. Khanwilkar, Dinesh Maheshwari and C.T. Ravikumar upheld the 2020 amendments to the FCRA, including the bar on transfer of foreign contributions to other entities, the mandatory SBI New Delhi account and the cap on administrative expenses. The Court held that receiving foreign contribution is not an absolute right.
items.why: Tightens the regulatory regime for NGOs receiving foreign funds.

items.headline: BCI identifies around 500 sub-standard law colleges for surprise inspections, closure if deficient
items.text: In a reply in the Rajya Sabha, the Law Ministry said the Bar Council of India had earmarked about 500 law colleges as sub-standard. Teams of former judges, senior advocates and academics would inspect them, and the BCI's Legal Education Committee would close institutions lacking faculty or infrastructure.

items.headline: Parliament passes Criminal Procedure (Identification) Bill, 2022 allowing collection of biometrics
items.text: The Rajya Sabha passed the Criminal Procedure (Identification) Bill, 2022, completing its passage through Parliament. It replaces the Identification of Prisoners Act, 1920 and allows police and prison officials to collect measurements such as finger and palm prints, iris and retina scans and biological samples from convicts and arrested persons, with records retained for 75 years.
items.why: Significantly widens state power to collect biometric data, raising privacy concerns.

items.headline: Lok Sabha passes Weapons of Mass Destruction (Amendment) Bill, 2022 barring financing of prohibited activities
items.text: The Lok Sabha passed the Weapons of Mass Destruction and their Delivery Systems (Prohibition of Unlawful Activities) Amendment Bill, 2022 a day after its introduction. The Bill amends the 2005 Act to bar persons from financing any prohibited activity relating to weapons of mass destruction and their delivery systems.

items.headline: Parliament passes Delhi Municipal Corporation (Amendment) Bill, 2022 to unify the three MCDs
items.text: The Rajya Sabha passed the Delhi Municipal Corporation (Amendment) Bill, 2022 on April 5, after Lok Sabha approval on March 30. The Bill merges the North, South and East Delhi municipal corporations into a single Municipal Corporation of Delhi and caps the number of seats at 250.
items.why: Restructures municipal governance in the national capital and shifts key powers to the Centre.

items.headline: Supreme Court strikes down Tamil Nadu's 10.5% internal quota for Vanniyars (Pattali Makkal Katchi v. A. Mayilerumperumal)
items.text: A bench of Justices L Nageswara Rao and BR Gavai upheld the Madras High Court's ruling that Tamil Nadu's 2021 Act giving 10.5% internal reservation to Vanniyakula Kshatriyas within the MBC quota violated Articles 14, 15 and 16 for want of substantial justification, and held that the 105th Constitutional Amendment is prospective.

items.headline: Supreme Court upholds Centre's One Rank One Pension policy (Indian Ex-Servicemen Movement v. Union of India)
items.text: In Indian Ex-Servicemen Movement v. Union of India (W.P.(C) No. 419/2016), a bench of Justices DY Chandrachud, Surya Kant and Vikram Nath found no constitutional infirmity in the OROP scheme as notified on 7 November 2015, rejecting the claim that all same-rank pensioners must draw identical pensions irrespective of retirement date.
items.why: Settled a long-running dispute affecting lakhs of defence pensioners.

items.headline: CLAT 2022 postponed from May 8 to June 19; application deadline extended to May 9
items.text: The Executive Committee of the Consortium of National Law Universities rescheduled CLAT-2022 for UG and PG programmes to 19 June 2022 (2 to 4 PM) and extended the last date for online applications to 9 May 2022.

items.headline: Supreme Court clears release of 'Gangubai Kathiawadi', says hurt sensibilities are not defamation
items.text: In Shri Babuji Rawji Shah v. S. Hussain Zaidi (2022 LiveLaw (SC) 213), the Supreme Court declined to stay the film 'Gangubai Kathiawadi', holding that a film does not become defamatory merely because it hurts sensibilities and that CBFC certification indicates the film is lawful.

items.headline: RERA prevails over SARFAESI; homebuyers can approach RERA against bank recovery (Union Bank of India v. Rajasthan RERA)
items.text: In Union Bank of India v. Rajasthan Real Estate Regulatory Authority (2022 LiveLaw (SC) 171), the Supreme Court held that in case of conflict the RERA Act prevails over the SARFAESI Act, so homebuyers can move the RERA authority against a bank's recovery action on a project, and RERA can entertain complaints against secured creditors.
items.why: Significant protection for homebuyers against lender enforcement.

items.headline: Bar Council of India declares AIBE XVI results
items.text: The Bar Council of India declared the results of the All India Bar Examination XVI, which had been held on 31 October 2021. Candidates who pass receive a Certificate of Practice from the BCI.

items.headline: Supreme Court: disobedience must be wilful for civil contempt under Order XXXIX Rule 2A CPC (Future Coupons v. Amazon)
items.text: In Future Coupons Pvt. Ltd. v. Amazon.com NV Investment Holdings LLC (2022 LiveLaw (SC) 114), the Supreme Court held that action under Order XXXIX Rule 2A of the CPC requires wilful disobedience of an injunction, in the long-running Future-Amazon dispute over the Future Retail-Reliance deal.

items.headline: Supreme Court quashes one-year suspension of 12 BJP MLAs by Maharashtra Assembly (Ashish Shelar v. Maharashtra Legislative Assembly)
items.text: In Ashish Shelar v. Maharashtra Legislative Assembly (W.P.(C) No. 797/2021), a bench of Justices AM Khanwilkar, Dinesh Maheshwari and CT Ravikumar held the resolution suspending 12 MLAs for a year unconstitutional, ruling that suspension cannot extend beyond the ongoing session as it effectively leaves constituencies unrepresented.
items.why: Sets limits on a legislature's power to discipline its members.

items.headline: Supreme Court upholds OBC and EWS quota in NEET All India Quota (Neil Aurelio Nunes v. Union of India)
items.text: Giving reasons for its 7 January 2022 order, a bench of Justices DY Chandrachud and AS Bopanna in Neil Aurelio Nunes v. Union of India (W.P.(C) No. 961/2021) upheld 27% OBC reservation in the All India Quota for medical admissions, holding that merit cannot be reduced to performance in a competitive examination and that reservation furthers substantive equality.
items.why: Important restatement of the relationship between merit and reservation.

items.headline: Supreme Court upholds winding up of Devas Multimedia for fraud (Devas Multimedia v. Antrix Corporation)
items.text: A bench of Justices Hemant Gupta and V Ramasubramanian dismissed Devas Multimedia's appeal and upheld the NCLT and NCLAT orders winding it up under Section 271(c) of the Companies Act, 2013, holding that where a company's affairs are conducted fraudulently as a continuing process, the right to seek winding up recurs and is not time-barred.
